SERVICE.what: The notice package recites the form's own certification line, that under G.L. 1956 Sec. 12-1-12.1(b)(1) or Sec. 12-1.3-3(a) the Office of the Attorney General AND the police department that originally brought the charge have been notified, and that the court date is at least ten (10) days after they were notified. It sets out the order of events explicitly - file, clerk sets the date at least ten days out, then give notice, then complete the certification - and warns that this is not the order the page reads in. It directs the participant to the clerk of the District Court division for how that division expects notice to be given and for the addresses, rather than inventing either. It also records that good moral character and rehabilitation are findings for the court and that nothing in the packet asserts them.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.what: The strongest fee handling I have read on this route, and it is the passage that most distinguishes this packet from its sibling. It gives the Superior Court's published no-fee answer, names the source and the exact FAQ question, and then refuses to extend it: 'Your case is in the DISTRICT COURT, and no District Court filing-fee schedule is held by this repository. The Superior Court's no-fee answer does not establish what the District Court charges, if anything, for this motion, and no District Court figure is printed here because none is held.' It declines to revive a $100 charge that older material describes and the current text of Sec. 12-1.3-3(c) does not carry, declines to apply the civil filing-fee schedule, and directs the participant to ask the clerk of the District Court division before going. It separates the filing fee from fines, costs and restitution, records that those may be waived or reduced by court order, and says that inability to pay is a question for the court rather than a reason to swear they are paid. The $5 BCI charge is identified as a charge for the record and expressly not a court filing fee. No fee, deadline, clerk practice or waiver rule is fabricated anywhere.

crossChecks.nearCloneObservation: These two Rhode Island tracks are close cousins and a reader should see the numbers rather than only the verdict. Per-page text similarity between the two delivered canonical packets is 0.912 on page 1 and 0.937 on page 2, falling to 0.483 on page 3 and 0.556 on page 4. More striking, the added-ink counts against their own DIFFERENT pinned sources are identical on page 3 - 15,843 canonical and 28,464 boundary on BOTH families - and differ by only 22 pixels on page 2. That is because Superior-55 and DC-33 are the same instrument issued for two courts, with the same caption geometry, so the same two participant facts render to nearly the same ink. It is a property of the forms, not evidence that the packets are the same. What distinguishes the two DELIVERED packets is substantive and adequate: different court (District v Superior, in the order caption and throughout the guide), different official form (DC-33 v Superior-55, different digests), different affidavit part (Part Three A: Single Conviction v Part Three: Deferred Sentence), different statutory authority (12-1.3-2 / 12-1.3-1 / 12-1.3-3 v 12-19-19 and 12-1.3-2(e)), different legal name, different page counts (15 v 14), different selection-control counts (37 v 33), and this packet's extra passage refusing to apply the Superior Court's no-fee answer to a District Court filing. They are not the same filing and neither is a clone of the other.

recordsThatDisagree.disagreement: The comment added to the builder says the siblings' byte-non-effect 'this lane measured rather than assumed'. Its own row says the opposite and more honestly: their fixtures were NOT rebuilt, and the non-effect is established by reading the flag's scope.
recordsThatDisagree.whichIMeasuredAgainst: The flag's scope, read myself, and the row's version is correct. preserveUnwrittenSelectionBackgrounds is a destructured parameter defaulting to false at every entry point - rcap-active-content.mjs lines 1320 and 1514, rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs line 1037 - so passing false explicitly is byte-equivalent to not passing it, and the key is absent on all three siblings. I could not rebuild the siblings to prove it (their directories are outside this sparse checkout and they belong to live lanes) and I did not try. Both commits touch only their own two family directories, the fix134 return files and the builder, so no sibling's committed bytes moved, and no shared module was edited.
recordsThatDisagree.onlyTheseTwoFamiliesMoved: Confirmed at the commit level: git show --stat on b2172c3bc and cf086ff03 lists no path under any other family's overlay directory.

recordsThatDisagree.record: FIX134's artifacts glyph readings against this family's own reports/actual-writes.json
recordsThatDisagree.disagreement: Under the identical key name addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes, FIX134's row reports 56 canonical / 98 boundary while the family's committed reports/actual-writes.json reports 126 canonical / 258 boundary.
recordsThatDisagree.whichIMeasuredAgainst: Both. They are two different quantities wearing one name: 56/98 is what classify-flattened-widget-appearances.mjs returns over flattened widget appearances only, which I reproduced exactly; 126/258 is the builder's count, which also takes in the composed pages. Neither is a fabricated zero, but the shared key name would show a downstream reader a discrepancy that is not one. I recorded 56/98 and named the tool.
recordsThatDisagree.andBothFamiliesReportIdenticalValuesHere: reports/actual-writes.json is identical on the two families for every one of these numbers - 126, 258, 9 flattened appearances, 9 actual writes, 4 valuesReportedByFinalizer. That is expected given the same two facts on two near-identical forms, and it is not by itself a clone signal, but it does mean this report cannot distinguish the two families and should not be used to.

recordsThatDisagree.record: The 'MEASURED HERE AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED' note on this host, and FIX134's correction to it
recordsThatDisagree.disagreement: FIX134 recorded that the note's diagnosis of 'synthesis' was wrong and that the mechanism is stripWidgetBackground / stripOpaqueBackgroundPaint in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs, which is why suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders was inert.
recordsThatDisagree.whichIMeasuredAgainst: The module source, and my reading supports FIX134 completely. stripOpaqueBackgroundPaint at line 451 removes a leading fill at grey >= 0.9 whose rectangle covers at least 90% of the widget /BBox - exactly the '1 g 0 0 W H re f' each source stream begins with. restrictWidgetContributions calls stripWidgetBackground on the PRESERVE_SOURCE_APPEARANCE branch, whereas suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders is read only on the RENDER_PARTICIPANT_VALUE_ONLY_WHEN_WRITTEN branch and inside neutralizeSynthesizedBorderCharacteristics. It never reaches the branch where the strip happens, so it could not have fixed this and was correctly not set. Nothing generates the stream: it is the court's own stream with one operator removed, which my raw SHA-256 match confirms. FIX133's independent finding of the same mechanism on Pennsylvania is consistent with this.
recordsThatDisagree.whatThisMeansForTheNoteStillInTheTree: The note at ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set still says the appearances are 'synthesis rather than misplacement' and that closing it needs a reader who can name the shared step. That reader has now been found twice. The note is stale, the sibling almost certainly carries the same uncovered-box defect, and it is the Captain's to widen - not mine, and not this lane's.

FIX134 called that 'a limit of this worktree, not a finding about those families', which is correct, and I repeat it rather than generalising from the exit code.

Its governance keys survived: the five non-artifact-bound keys are present, and the acceptanceReceipt bound to the superseded canonical bebf3cd9... is recorded as withdrawn under acceptanceReceiptWithdrawn carrying both digests, not deleted and not relabelled as covering the new output. I make no claim about the 251 files I could not read.

It restored the court's own opaque check-box mask inside the notarial certificate of a sworn affidavit instead of deleting the court's bevels, which is what the dispatch it was given would have caused. Every number it reported reproduces exactly. This FAIL is for a different and older defect on a different component, which its repair never touched and never claimed to.
